summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for hematemesis and septic shock in the setting of HCV cirrhosis and portopulmonary hypertension. He presented with acute gastrointestinal bleeding from esophageal varices, profound neutropenia that rapidly evolved into leukocytosis, and respiratory distress. A tunnelled central line was removed as a suspected source of bloodstream infection, and he was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, later narrowed based on negative cultures. He required two therapeutic paracenteses for symptomatic ascites, placement of a PICC line for remodulin, and a Dobhoff tube for nutritional support. During the hospitalization, he developed an NSTEMI with nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, confirmed by rising troponins and EKG changes, leading to transfer to the ICU and subsequent cardiac catheterization, which showed a distal PDA cutoff without need for intervention. He stabilized over 12 days, with resolution of infection, improved respiratory status, and no further bleeding. He was discharged home on all home medications with plans for outpatient follow-up in pulmonology, cardiology, and transplant, and scheduled blood cultures to guide future line management.
